title: Poulet Mafé
localName: Poulet mafé — à la sauce d’arachide
author: Amina Savoura
desc: Chicken browned with onions and chile, simmered in a peanut-paste sauce seasoned with nététou — the only mafé in this collection that uses a fermented seasoning.
longDesc: A short, home-kitchen mafé from the Afrik cooking pages. Chicken pieces are browned in oil, onions and chile are added until the onions turn golden, then garlic for two minutes and tomato concentrate for two more. Peanut paste (the page names Dakatine as one brand), a teaspoon of nététou, salt, pepper and a litre of water go in, and everything simmers gently for 30 to 45 minutes with a kilo of mixed vegetables — carrot, potato, pumpkin, aubergine, sweet potato, cabbage. There is no acid and no okra, and the nététou — pre-fermented locust-bean seasoning — is what gives it a savoury edge.
ingredients: 1 chicken, cut up — weight not printed
200 g peanut paste (the page says ‘Dakatine or other’)
1 kg vegetables of your choice, alone or mixed: carrots, potatoes, pumpkin, aubergines, sweet potatoes, cabbage, etc.
2 small tins of tomato concentrate — tin size not printed
1 teaspoon nététou (fermented locust-bean seasoning, bought ready-made)
Oil, salt, pepper — quantities not printed
equipment: Mortar or bowl for crushing garlic
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the chicken pieces.
Add the sliced onions and the chile and cook until the onions are golden.
Add the crushed garlic and cook 2 minutes so the garlic takes colour, then the tomato concentrate and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the peanut paste, nététou, salt, pepper and 1 litre of water. Cook everything over low heat for 30 to 45 minutes.
Add the vegetables according to how long they take — firm ones (carrot, cassava, pumpkin) with the liquid, soft ones (aubergine, cabbage) later — and cook until tender.
chefTips: ‘Until the onions are golden’ and ‘so that the garlic browns’ are the two colour cues in the original — both better guides than the stopwatch.
Nététou is added in small quantity, one teaspoon here. It is pungent and salty; taste before adding more salt.
Keep the heat low once the peanut paste goes in, or the paste can scorch on the bottom of the pot.
Add the vegetable pieces in stages; the printed method does not stage them, so this is a cook’s adjustment, not a printed step.
commonMistakes: High heat after the peanut paste is in.
Adding all vegetables at once so the soft ones disintegrate.
reheating: Low heat with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Peanut paste is a good source of protein and healthy fats.
A kilo of mixed vegetables gives fibre and a spread of vitamins.
culturalNote: One of the claims in the sources is that mafé arrived in Senegal from Mali; Fine Dining Lovers (Mathilde Bourge, 2018) puts it in a single sentence — ‘a dish from Mali adapted to Senegalese cuisine’ — with no citation. No other source in this collection makes or contradicts that claim.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Poulet mafé (à la sauce d’arachide)’. Byline exactly as printed: ‘Amina Savoura’. Publication: Afrik. Date as printed: ‘Publié le 21 octobre 2010 à 12h54’. Yield as printed: ‘Pour 4 à 6 personnes’. Times as printed: preparation 30 mn, cooking 45 mn. TWO-PASS.

ONE TEXTUAL DISAGREEMENT between passes, recorded: pass one read the peanut paste line as ‘pâte d’ararchides’ (doubled r), pass two as ‘pâte d’arachides’. The quantity (200 g) agrees; the spelling does not. Neither is picked.

ABSENT, not estimated: the weight of the chicken, the size of the tomato-concentrate tins, and quantities of oil, salt and pepper. The page spells the seasoning ‘netatou (épice)’ — a fifth variant spelling in this collection.
The page repeats its own error once: step 2 reads ‘les oignons émincés et et le piment’ (doubled ‘et’). Recorded as printed.

The vegetable staging in the steps here is an editorial reading, not printed: the original says only that the peanut paste, nététou, salt, pepper and water are added and everything cooks gently for 30 to 45 minutes.

DISAGREEMENT with SEN022 and SEN024, unreconciled: the Saveur printing uses lime juice, okra, cabbage and a reduction step; this Afrik version uses nététou, no acid, no okra, and simmers without reducing. It is the only mafé printing in the set with a fermented seasoning.
